selection_rule: Select credential-free, deterministic scenarios whose breakage would remove a user-visible route, branch, visible tool, permission boundary, or MCP behavior. Inputs and rationale live here; responses are always captured from the current code.

http.expansion: For every path×method in baseline/l1/opencrab-l1.json, capture a normal/local-precondition probe and an input-rejection or resource-absence probe. Normal branches that require an external credential, live service, LLM, or operator workspace are emitted as uncollected L3 entries.
why: A replacement must not silently drop an HTTP method that remains present in the L1 route inventory.
Malformed JSON and missing-resource behavior are consumed by the dashboard and integrations, not just happy-path payloads.
Fresh seeded state per probe prevents ordering from becoming part of the contract.

dimensions: depth: 0, 1, and the depth-2 spawn cap
configured feature: shell enabled and disabled
run allowlist across core, gateway, and MCP slots
tool_visibility.why: These are the independent gates used by the production executor before the LLM sees definitions.

selected_facets: empty arguments for every observed tool whose live schema declares required fields
direct-call permission rejection for every observed owner-only, trusted-only, and trusted-only-MCP tool
contained successful calls spanning core read/control, workspace mutation, task state, system gateway reads, and MCP
MCP tool-declared failure and forwarding/transport failure
tool_execution.why: Visibility alone does not prove direct invocation is gated or that result/error translation survives a replacement.
tool_execution.non_selected_success_policy: A tool without a credential-free and side-effect-contained successful scenario is emitted as uncollected instead of being called with guessed arguments.

success_fixture.workspace: A fresh temporary workspace contains no operator files. The cases create captured/, captured/file.txt, captured/summary.txt, and skills/captured-skill.skill.md through the real tools; the shell allowlist contains only printf.
success_fixture.core_db: A fresh in-memory DB contains agent baseline-agent, two fixed session logs for baseline-session (ids 1 and 2), active owner-created skill Seed Skill, topic t1, declared units u1/u2, condensed cores m1/m2, and category nodes c1/c2/c3. Fixed timestamps and IDs are used only as preconditions; tool-created IDs come from the implementation and are normalized after capture.
success_fixture.gateway_db: A separate fresh in-memory AppState DB contains baseline-agent and a disabled Nostr row with a deterministic non-production fixture nsec. No production credential, operator workspace, network service, or live gateway is used.
success_fixture.session: Gateway self-management calls use web-baseline-agent-conversation so the production TimedFire descriptor resolves a real local web session target. History reads use baseline-session.
success_fixture.subtasks: cancel_subtask, steer_subtask, and report_progress receive an in-memory running SubtaskRegistry entry with id baseline-subtask, parent web-baseline-agent-conversation, sub-session subtask-baseline-subtask, an actual pending Tokio abort handle, owner caller, and the real lifecycle latch. spawn_subtask receives a real registry and runs the real spawn path; its background LLM run has no provider and is not represented as a successful completion.
success_fixture.mcp: Two in-memory McpServer implementations expose public_local/echo and trusted_local/echo. Calls traverse the real McpToolProvider and BridgedExecutor.

success_uncollected_l3.nostr_generate_key: Requires the operator's nostaro executable and writes key material outside the temporary workspace.
success_uncollected_l3.nostr_switch_identity: Requires a generated key and configured Nostr transport capability; successful adoption may start a live relay connection.
success_uncollected_l3.nostr_run: Requires an adopted identity, operator nostaro executable, and potentially live relay/service I/O.
success_uncollected_l3.run_my_heartbeat: Successful manual fire runs an actual agent turn through a configured transport and LLM provider.
success_uncollected_l3.request_peer_review: Success delivers a message through the active transport. A local fake delivery would not fix live delivery behavior.

mcp.why: This exercises the real MCP framing/parser without a production credential, subprocess package, network, or external server.
